section_summary: This section records requests and official responses concerning Japanese naval transports calling at Los Angeles for crude petroleum in 1941. State Department correspondence addresses their status as public naval vessels, port courtesies, crew landings, and, after the July freezing order, the licenses required to load oil. Internal memoranda and a newspaper clipping examine the transports’ customs exemptions, the frequency of their visits, and possible security concerns.

subfiles.title: Notice to Navy concerning Kokuyo Maru visit

subfiles.title: Policy questions raised by Erimo visit

subfiles.summary: The division recommends sending preliminary Erimo communications while Customs and other offices investigate the exemptions enjoyed by Japanese naval transports.

subfiles.title: Shiriya visit and freezing-order memorandum
subfiles.about: Recommends approving Shiriya’s visit while explaining new export-license requirements.
subfiles.summary: The governor and Navy have asked whether the freezing order permits Shiriya to load crude oil. The division recommends allowing entry but telling Japan and California that oil exports require individual Treasury licenses as well as normal export-control licenses.

subfiles.title: Treasury customs authorization for Shiriya
subfiles.about: Authorizes customary customs facilities for Shiriya.
subfiles.summary: Treasury instructs the Los Angeles collector to extend courtesies for the August 9–14 visit.

subfiles.title: Shiriya visit request
subfiles.about: Requests a Los Angeles oil-loading visit for Shiriya.
subfiles.summary: The ambassador proposes August 9–14 under Captain Tarohachi Shinoda and asks about crew landing.

subfiles.title: Telegram to California on Shiriya oil loading
subfiles.about: Explains that Shiriya needs a specific license to load crude oil.
subfiles.summary: State cites the order adding Japan to freezing controls and the need for Treasury authorization.

subfiles.summary: State encloses the Japanese request and asks for customary facilities absent objection.

subfiles.title: Conditional approval for Shiriya
subfiles.about: Approves Shiriya’s visit and crew landing while setting oil-loading conditions.
subfiles.summary: State permits the visit but says loading crude petroleum requires a Treasury license under the freezing order and a State Department export license. Each application will be considered on its merits.

subfiles.summary: The governor seeks clarification following the freezing order.

subfiles.title: Questions on Japanese transport exemptions
subfiles.about: Lists questions arising from a San Francisco Chronicle account of Japanese tankers.
subfiles.summary: The division asks which port charges, inspections, customs procedures, and cargo checks public vessels avoid, and whether the newspaper’s oil-shipment claims are accurate.

subfiles.title: U.S. Oil Is Ferried to Japan
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese naval tankers carrying American oil under public-vessel privileges.
subfiles.summary: The article claims the tankers avoid port fees and routine customs inspection, describes oil shipments from San Francisco and nearby ports, and names several vessels.

subfiles.title: Duplicate oil-tanker clipping
subfiles.about: Repeats the article on Japanese naval tankers and American oil.
subfiles.summary: A second copy of the clipping discusses customs immunity, port charges, and tanker movements.

subfiles.title: Analysis of public-vessel immunity and port charges
subfiles.about: Answers questions about customs exemptions and tanker charges.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum estimates that a commercial Toei Maru would pay $354.20 per call under applicable rates, while Japanese public vessels pay no port charges. It explains the limited customs supervision of foreign public vessels and says available records cannot confirm all newspaper claims or precise oil volumes.

subfiles.title: Referral of proposed six-month schedule request
subfiles.about: Recommends Navy review of a draft request for Japanese transport schedules.
subfiles.summary: The author notes differing Navy views and possible Japanese reciprocal demands.

subfiles.title: Draft-note procedure for transport schedules
subfiles.about: Clarifies that advance schedules would not replace individual visit requests.
subfiles.summary: The division recommends holding its draft note to Japan until Navy comments formally.

subfiles.title: Frequency and security of Japanese transport visits
subfiles.about: Evaluates whether repeated Japanese naval transport visits abuse public-vessel courtesies.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum reviews Navy concerns that frequent visits and limited inspection could facilitate espionage, while noting that export controls govern oil shipments and port-fee exemptions are relatively small. It considers refusing some visits but doubts this would materially reduce oil exports. It recommends asking Japan for an approximate six-month visit schedule, then consulting Navy on any calls deemed inconvenient.
